title: Infinite Symmetry Algebras in Four-Dimensional Conformal Field Theories
summary: In generic interacting four-dimensional Lorentzian conformal field theories, an infinite set of universal light-ray operators constructed from the stress tensor is shown to generate the wedge subalgebra of the loop algebra of ${\rm w}_{1+\infty}$. This algebra was recently identified among the asymptotic symmetries of asymptotically flat spacetimes. The one-point functions of the ${\rm w}_{1+\infty}$ generators in scalar states (also known as one-point event shapes) are explicitly demonstrated to be finite and are precisely related to universal soft factors in the infinite tower of soft graviton theorems. A second universal class of light-ray operators that generates the ''$S$ algebra,'' the gauge-theoretic analog of ${\rm w}_{1+\infty}$, is also constructed and shown to have finite one-point functions in four-dimensional conformal field theories with a spin-one conserved current. Along with the details of these results, this paper presents a general classification of stress-tensor and conserved current light-ray operators by scaling dimension and Lorentz ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{C})$ weights, a general technique for computing commutators by Poincaré recursion, results for other light-ray operator algebras including a local version of the four-dimensional conformal symmetry algebra, and examples for free scalar fields.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that universal light-ray operators built from the stress tensor in 4D Lorentzian CFTs generate the wedge subalgebra of the loop algebra of w_{1+∞}, which has been identified among asymptotic symmetries of asymptotically flat spacetimes. The one-point functions of these generators in scalar states are finite and precisely match universal soft factors in the infinite tower of soft graviton theorems. A gauge-theoretic analog (the "S algebra") is also constructed from conserved current light-ray operators with finite one-point functions.
AI.motivation: To establish precise connections between bulk gravitational symmetries (asymptotic symmetries of flat spacetime, including the w_{1+∞} loop algebra) and boundary CFT data, by constructing explicit light-ray operators in generic interacting 4D CFTs that realize these infinite-dimensional algebras and verifying their physical finiteness and relation to soft theorems.
AI.method: The paper develops a general classification of stress-tensor and conserved-current light-ray operators by scaling dimension and Lorentz SL(2,C) weights. It introduces a Poincaré recursion technique for computing commutators of these operators, and constructs the w_{1+∞} loop algebra wedge subalgebra from stress-tensor light-ray operators and the S algebra from current light-ray operators. Free scalar field examples are provided to illustrate the constructions.
AI.result: The one-point functions of the w_{1+∞} generators in scalar states are shown to be finite and precisely related to universal soft factors in the infinite tower of soft graviton theorems. Both the w_{1+∞} algebra (from stress tensor) and S algebra (from conserved current) light-ray operators have finite one-point functions and form well-defined algebras in generic interacting 4D CFTs. A local version of the 4D conformal symmetry algebra is also obtained.
AI.conclusion: Universal light-ray operators in 4D CFTs realize the loop algebra of w_{1+∞} and its gauge-theoretic analog, connecting CFT observables directly to flat-space asymptotic symmetries and soft graviton theorems, providing a concrete holographic/dictionary between boundary correlators and bulk soft physics.

title: Towers of Operators in CFTs and Convexity Bounds at Large Charge
summary: In arXiv:2406.19441, it was shown that for 3d CFTs with a moduli space along which a $U(1)$ symmetry is spontaneously broken, the minimum scaling dimension at large charge $Q$ scales as $Δ_{\min}(Q)=α_1 Q+α_0+O(1/Q)$. Motivated by the holographic swampland program, we study possible bounds on the coefficients $α_i$. For $α_0$, the weak gravity conjecture motivates the CFT charge convexity conjecture, which requires the bound $α_0\leq 0$. Using the moduli space EFT we prove this bound for the $\textit{projected}$ $Δ_{\min}(Q)$, obtained by fixing a single charge $Q$ and minimizing the dimension while allowing all other charges to vary. This provides a WGC-motivated bound that is explicitly provable using CFT methods. On the other hand, we show that $α_1$ admits no universal bound apart from the trivial bound $α_1\geq 0$. We also compute $α_1$ and $α_0$ in several new 3d $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories via the $ε$-expansion and large-$N$ methods.

AI.tldr: This paper studies bounds on the coefficients of the large-charge scaling dimension expansion Δ_min(Q) = α₁Q + α₀ + O(1/Q) in 3D CFTs. Using moduli space EFT methods, it proves the weak gravity conjecture-motivated charge convexity bound α₀ ≤ 0 for the projected Δ_min(Q), while showing α₁ admits no universal bound beyond α₁ ≥ 0. New α₁ and α₀ values are computed in 3D N=1 theories via ε-expansion and large-N methods.
AI.motivation: The holographic swampland program seeks to constrain consistent quantum gravity and CFT data. The paper is motivated by testing whether the weak gravity conjecture (WGC) implies constraints on large-charge data in 3D CFTs, specifically the coefficients α₁ and α₀ in the large-charge scaling dimension expansion. Proving or disproving such bounds via explicit CFT methods connects swampland constraints to provable CFT statements.
AI.method: The paper uses the moduli space effective field theory (EFT) framework to analyze the large-charge sector of 3D CFTs with spontaneously broken U(1) symmetry. It proves the bound α₀ ≤ 0 for the projected Δ_min(Q) (minimizing dimension over all other charges while fixing a single charge Q) using moduli space EFT methods, and constructs arguments showing α₁ has no universal upper bound. Computations of α₁ and α₀ are performed in 3D N=1 theories using ε-expansion around 4−ε dimensions and large-N techniques.
AI.result: The paper proves α₀ ≤ 0 for the projected large-charge scaling dimension, providing an explicitly provable WGC-motivated bound using CFT methods. It demonstrates that α₁ admits no universal bound beyond the trivial α₁ ≥ 0, ruling out stronger swampland-inspired constraints on α₁. New explicit values of α₁ and α₀ are computed for various 3D N=1 theories via ε-expansion and large-N methods.
AI.conclusion: The charge convexity conjecture (α₀ ≤ 0) is proven for projected Δ_min(Q) using moduli space EFT, strengthening the connection between the weak gravity conjecture and CFT constraints. However, α₁ cannot be universally bounded nontrivially, meaning the WGC-motivated bounds only apply to the subleading large-charge coefficient, not the leading one. The new N=1 computations provide concrete data to test these bounds.

title: From Horizon Microstates to the Black Hole Membrane
summary: The membrane paradigm represents a black-hole horizon by a fictitious conducting surface. We derive a microscopic electromagnetic membrane from black-hole matrix quantum mechanics. The fuzzy-sphere horizon carries a Berry monopole, placing its fundamental fermionic partons in lowest-Landau-level states with Ohmic and Hall responses. Off-diagonal bifundamental modes connecting the horizon and exterior matrix blocks become tachyonic near the horizon and condense, dynamically coupling the horizon gauge field to the exterior Maxwell field. In the low-frequency regime $ωR\ll1$, the fixed-parton transport description predicts frequency- and helicity-dependent reflectivity. At larger frequency, real parton excitations require a black-hole $S$-matrix. Ohm's law then fixes the inclusive absorption probability; unitarity bounds the local absorption cross section by the horizon area, with the classical conductivity $1/4π$ saturating this maximal-absorption bound.

Tachyonic bifundamental modes condense near the horizon, coupling the horizon gauge field to the exterior Maxwell field, yielding frequency- and helicity-dependent reflectivity in the low-frequency regime and an absorption cross section bounded by the horizon area, with the classical conductivity 1/4π saturating the maximal-absorption bound.

AI.method: The authors use matrix quantum mechanics of black holes. title: Chiral symmetry and curvature bounds in de Sitter spacetime
summary: We study chiral symmetry breaking in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model on a de Sitter background, treating it as a non-renormalizable effective field theory with a physical ultraviolet cutoff. Using exponential proper-time regularization, we obtain an exact solution for the constituent fermion mass in the strong-curvature regime via the Lambert $W$ function. The consistency condition for real-valued solutions leads to an upper bound on the cosmological constant, indicating a limitation of the mean-field description rather than a fundamental physical constraint on the spacetime geometry.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates chiral symmetry breaking in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model on a de Sitter background using exponential proper-time regularization, deriving an exact closed-form solution for the constituent fermion mass via the Lambert W function in the strong-curvature regime, and showing that real-valued solutions impose an upper bound on the cosmological constant—interpreted as a limitation of mean-field theory rather than a physical constraint on spacetime.
AI.motivation: To understand how curvature affects chiral symmetry breaking in a strongly interacting fermion system, treating the NJL model as a non-renormalizable effective field theory with a physical UV cutoff on curved spacetime (de Sitter background).
AI.method: The NJL model is studied on de Sitter spacetime as an effective field theory with a physical ultraviolet cutoff. Exponential proper-time regularization is employed, and the gap equation is solved exactly in the strong-curvature regime using the Lambert W function.
AI.result: An exact solution for the constituent fermion mass is obtained in terms of the Lambert W function. The requirement of real-valued solutions yields an upper bound on the cosmological constant, which reflects a limitation of the mean-field approximation rather than a fundamental restriction on de Sitter geometry.
AI.conclusion: The curvature-induced upper bound on the cosmological constant is an artifact of the mean-field description. The physical interpretation is that the NJL model provides a consistent effective description of chiral symmetry breaking on de Sitter space up to a certain curvature scale, beyond which the mean-field approach breaks down.

title: Natural Phantom Crossing from Axion-WIMP Interactions
summary: We construct a technically natural model in which thermal dark matter (DM) interacts with axion dark energy (DE) and produces an apparent late-time crossing of the phantom divide. A direct axion coupling to weakly-interacting massive particles (WIMPs) would ordinarily radiatively destabilize the ultralight axion potential. We avoid this issue through $N$ fermion species related by a cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry, which projects the leading Coleman-Weinberg potential onto the exponentially suppressed $N$th harmonic. Although the microscopic theory preserves $\mathbb{Z}_N$, the axion-dependent WIMP masses generate unequal equilibrium abundances that freeze-out imprints on the cosmological relic state, thereby breaking the symmetry spontaneously. The resulting relic distribution retains a memory of the initial axion value and generates an unsuppressed finite-density potential that holds the field fixed at early times. As the WIMP density dilutes, the axion rolls toward the minimum of its confining potential, transferring energy from DE to DM at late times. An observer assuming separately conserved components then infers an effective equation of state that crosses below $-1$, without ghosts or violation of the null-energy condition. We present an illustrative cosmological solution with a DESI-like phantom crossing and percent-level suppression of structure growth, and discuss the implications of the WIMP multiplicity and relic distribution for DM searches.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a technically natural model connecting thermal WIMP dark matter to axion dark energy via a cyclic Z_N symmetry. The symmetry protects the ultralight axion potential from radiative destabilization, while the axion-dependent WIMP masses generate unequal freeze-out abundances that break the symmetry spontaneously. As WIMP density dilutes, the axion rolls and transfers energy from DE to DM, producing an apparent phantom-crossing equation of state without ghosts. The model yields a DESI-like phantom crossing and percent-level suppression of structure growth.
AI.motivation: A direct axion coupling to WIMPs would ordinarily radiatively destabilize the ultralight axion potential, making such a coupling technically unnatural. The authors aim to construct a natural model that couples dark matter to dark energy while avoiding this instability, and in doing so, explain the apparent late-time phantom-divide crossing suggested by cosmological observations (e.g., DESI) without introducing ghosts or violating the null-energy condition.
AI.method: The model introduces N fermion species related by a cyclic Z_N symmetry. This symmetry projects the leading Coleman-Weinberg radiative potential onto the exponentially suppressed Nth harmonic, preserving the ultralight axion mass. The axion-dependent WIMP masses yield unequal equilibrium abundances at freeze-out, spontaneously breaking Z_N. The relic distribution then generates an unsuppressed finite-density potential that pins the axion at early times; as WIMPs dilute, the axion rolls to its confining-potential minimum, transferring DE to DM. The authors present an illustrative cosmological solution exhibiting a DESI-like phantom crossing and percent-level suppression of structure growth.
AI.result: The model produces an apparent late-time crossing of the phantom divide in the effective equation of state without ghosts or violation of the null-energy condition. It yields a DESI-like phantom crossing and percent-level suppression of structure growth. The WIMP multiplicity and relic distribution have observable implications for dark matter searches.
AI.conclusion: A technically natural axion-DM coupling is achievable via Z_N symmetry, and the resulting late-time energy transfer between DE and DM can mimic phantom behavior observationally, with testable consequences for structure growth and DM detection.

title: Quantum Scattering in Schwarzschild Spacetime: Hawking Radiation and Black Hole Atmospheres
summary: In this paper, we investigate scattering of a scalar field near a Schwarzschild black hole through its $S$-matrix. Within this framework, we obtain a novel derivation of Hawking radiation by computing the emission rate, which yields a Bose--Einstein distribution with temperature $T_H=(8πGM)^{-1}$, the Hawking temperature. In addition to Hawking radiation, the S-matrix exhibits antibound states, corresponding to excitations at the threshold of becoming scattering (bound) states if the potential is decreased (increased). We interpret these excitations as constituents of the black-hole quantum atmosphere: a thermalised region outside of the event horizon, which is the source of the Hawking radiation. Using the spectrum of antibound states, we found the atmospheric radius, $r_{\text{Atm}} \approx 2.77 r_{s}$, which is in good agreement with previous results in the literature obtained through other methods. Our results indicate that, at the macroscopic level, the quantum atmosphere behaves like an ordinary thermalised gas at the Hawking temperature.

AI.tldr: The paper studies scalar field scattering near a Schwarzschild black hole via its S-matrix, deriving Hawking radiation as Bose-Einstein emission with the Hawking temperature TH=(8πGM)^-1. The S-matrix reveals antibound states interpreted as constituents of a quantum atmosphere—a thermalized region outside the event horizon that sources the Hawking radiation—with an atmospheric radius r_Atm ≈ 2.77 r_s, consistent with prior literature.
AI.motivation: To provide a novel S-matrix-based derivation of Hawking radiation and to identify its physical source as a quantum atmosphere (described by antibound states), offering a microscopic framework for a previously established macroscopic picture.
AI.method: The authors compute the scalar-field S-matrix for scattering near a Schwarzschild black hole, extract the emission rate to derive the Hawking spectrum, and analyze the poles (antibound states) of the S-matrix to characterize the quantum atmosphere and determine its radius.
AI.result: The emission rate yields a Bose–Einstein distribution with the Hawking temperature. Antibound states are identified as quantum-atmosphere constituents, giving an atmospheric radius of approximately 2.77 r_s, in good agreement with earlier results from different methods.
AI.conclusion: The quantum atmosphere behaves macroscopically like an ordinary thermalized gas at the Hawking temperature, and the S-matrix framework provides a new, consistent route to deriving Hawking radiation and characterizing its source.

title: Gravity Probe-DM: The Gravitational Laboratory for Dark Matter
summary:
Dark matter is inferred gravitationally across the Universe but has not been detected within the Solar System. The Sun inevitably focuses incident unbound dark matter into an irreducible downstream wake. Its structure encodes the incoming density and velocity distribution and, for wave dark matter, the de Broglie scale. We propose Gravity Probe-DM, a heliocentric search using precision ranging between spacecrafts. The exact two-spacecraft observable is the differential wake acceleration; for a short baseline, it becomes the wake tidal tensor projected along the baseline.
  For a $2.5\times10^6\,\mathrm{km}$ baseline crossing a $0.1\,\mathrm{AU}$ coherent width at $30\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, a one-percent excess gives a raw uniform-core range scale of $0.63\,\mathrm{pm}$ over $5.77\,\mathrm d$. While the projected tide remains coherent over an interval $T$, the free response grows as $T^2$, reaching $2.5\,\mathrm{nm}$ over one year. An illustrative low-lag dark-disk component carrying $20\%$ of the reference local density and reaching a $30\%$ focused contrast gives a one-year scale of about $15\,\mathrm{nm}$. These pre-fit response scales show that trajectory design can move the signal from sub-picometre to nanometre scales.
  A detection would provide a purely gravitational map of local dark matter and probe the flow that produced it, including particle versus wave focusing. The Sun supplies the lens, spacecraft sample the wake, and precision ranging reads out its gravitational imprint.

AI.tldr: Propose Gravity Probe-DM: a heliocentric mission using precision inter-spacecraft ranging to detect gravitational focusing of dark matter by the Sun, forming a downstream wake whose structure encodes dark matter density, velocity distribution, and (for wave dark matter) the de Broglie scale.
AI.motivation: Dark matter has never been detected within the Solar System despite being inferred gravitationally everywhere else. The Sun's gravitational lensing necessarily focuses incident dark matter into a downstream wake; measuring this wake provides the first direct, purely gravitational probe of local dark matter.
AI.method: The exact two-spacecraft observable is the differential wake acceleration, which reduces to the projected wake tidal tensor for short baselines. Precision ranging between spacecraft in heliocentric orbits samples this tidal signal; trajectory design can amplify the free response from sub-picometre to nanometre scales via T² growth over coherent observation intervals.
AI.result: For a 2.5×10⁶ km baseline crossing a 0.1 AU coherent width at 30 km/s, a 1% density excess yields a 0.63 pm raw range scale over 5.77 days; the projected tide over one year reaches 2.5 nm. An illustrative low-lag dark-disk component (20% local density, 30% focused contrast) gives ~15 nm one-year scale.
AI.conclusion: A detection would yield a purely gravitational map of local dark matter and distinguish particle from wave focusing. The Sun acts as the lens, spacecraft sample the gravitational wake, and precision ranging reads out its imprint—demonstrating feasibility through trajectory design that moves signal scales into measurable regimes.

title: Line operator indices of S-fold theories
summary: We study superconformal indices in the presence of line operators in S-fold theories. We consider two types of lines, realized by fundamental strings and fivebranes, respectively, in AdS$_5 \times S^5/\mathbb{Z}_k$. For fundamental lines, we analyze the corresponding indices including finite-$N$ corrections arising from giant graviton configurations. For $k=2$, we compare the holographic results with line operator indices in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theories with orthogonal gauge groups. For $k=3,4$ and $6$, we focus on the rank $2$ case, in which the supersymmetry is enhanced to ${\cal N}=4$, and compare them with the corresponding Wilson-'t Hooft line operator indices. In both cases, we find improved agreement once giant graviton contributions are included. For line operators realized by fivebranes, after confirming agreement for $k=2$, we construct BPS configurations for $k\geq 3$ explicitly using fivebrane junctions and derive the indices in the large $N$ limit by the mode analysis on the fivebrane junctions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies superconformal indices in S-fold theories in the presence of line operators, considering two types: fundamental strings and fivebranes. For fundamental lines, finite-N giant graviton corrections improve agreement with N=4 SYM results (orthogonal gauge groups for k=2, rank-2 enhanced supersymmetry for k=3,4,6). For fivebrane line operators, BPS configurations are constructed via fivebrane junctions for k≥3, with large-N indices derived from mode analysis.
AI.motivation: To compute and understand superconformal indices in the presence of line operators in S-fold theories, which are holographically dual to AdS5 × S5/Zk geometries. The goal is to test and improve holographic agreement with gauge theory results, particularly regarding subtle finite-N effects and higher-rank line operator constructs.
AI.method: The authors analyze two types of line operators: (1) fundamental string lines, where they compute indices including finite-N giant graviton corrections, comparing with N=4 SYM Wilson-'t Hooft line operator indices for various k and gauge groups; (2) fivebrane lines, where they construct BPS configurations using fivebrane junctions and perform mode analysis on these junctions to derive indices in the large N limit.
AI.result: Improved agreement is found in both cases once giant graviton contributions are included. For k=2, results match N=4 SYM with orthogonal gauge groups. For k=3,4,6 (rank 2 theories with enhanced N=4 supersymmetry), agreement is achieved with Wilson-'t Hooft line operator indices. For fivebrane line operators, agreement is confirmed for k=2, and explicit BPS configurations and large-N indices are constructed for k≥3.
AI.conclusion: The inclusion of giant graviton contributions significantly improves the holographic computation of superconformal indices with line operators in S-fold theories, providing strong support for the AdS/CFT correspondence in these settings. The fivebrane junction approach successfully extends the analysis to higher k values.

title: Hadron Structure from the Hierarchy of Quantum Correlations in Deep-Inelastic Scattering
summary: We show that the hierarchy of quantum correlations produced in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) can serve as a novel probe of the proton's nonperturbative structure. Specifically, we show that quantum entanglement, discord, steering, and magic provide nontrivial and complementary sensitivities to the nucleon's parton distribution functions (PDFs), particularly those encoding the transverse-spin polarization of the interacting quark. This connection leads to a unique probe of the proton's parton-level tensor charges with implications for beyond Standard Model (BSM) physics searches. We propose how quantum information measures can be utilized for precision studies of hadron structure at DIS experiments like the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using quantum information measures (entanglement, discord, steering, magic) from deep-inelastic scattering to probe proton structure, particularly transverse-spin parton distributions and tensor charges, with implications for BSM physics and applications at the EIC.
AI.motivation: To develop a novel, complementary probe of the proton's nonperturbative structure using quantum correlations generated in DIS, which can access parton distribution functions and tensor charges in ways not achievable through conventional observables.
AI.method: The authors analyze the hierarchy of quantum correlations (entanglement, discord, steering, and magic) present in DIS and demonstrate how each provides distinct sensitivity to PDFs, especially those encoding transverse-spin polarization of interacting quarks.
AI.result: Each quantum information measure provides unique and complementary sensitivity to nucleon PDFs, particularly transverse-spin quark polarizations, enabling access to parton-level tensor charges relevant for BSM physics searches.
AI.conclusion: Quantum information measures can serve as a new precision tool for hadron structure studies at future facilities like the Electron-Ion Collider, connecting quantum information science with high-energy nuclear physics.

title: A Toy Model for Topological Entanglement Features in 1+1D Integrable Quantum Field Theory
summary: In this paper we investigate an entanglement measure, the Rényi entropy, in a 1+1D integrable quantum field theory known as the Federbush model. This is a deformation of the theory of two massive Dirac fermions by means of a bilinear term in the $U(1)$ currents that couples the two fermion species. This deformation gives rise to $S$-matrix elements which are coupling-dependent phases, distinct from $- 1$. These non-trivial phases can be seen as encoding anyon-like statistics. From this viewpoint, the Federbush model is a toy model for topological features of entanglement in one space dimension. In this paper we show that, for an infinite system, these topological features play no role when computing many known measures of entanglement at equilibrium in the ground state. This conclusion applies also to the post-quench dynamics after a small quench of the topological parameter.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes Rényi entropy in the Federbush model, a 1+1D integrable QFT that is a deformation of two massive Dirac fermions with coupling-dependent phase S-matrix elements encoding anyon-like statistics. The authors show that these topological features do not affect known entanglement measures in the ground state at equilibrium for an infinite system, nor do they affect post-quench dynamics after a small quench of the topological parameter.
AI.motivation: The Federbush model serves as a toy model to investigate whether non-trivial anyon-like topological statistics encoded in coupling-dependent S-matrix phases contribute to entanglement measures in one spatial dimension, aiming to understand topological features of entanglement in integrable quantum field theories.
AI.method: The authors compute Rényi entropy (and other known entanglement measures) in the Federbush model, an integrable QFT deformed from two massive Dirac fermions by a bilinear U(1) current coupling term. They analyze both the ground state at equilibrium in an infinite system and post-quench dynamics following a small quench of the topological parameter.
AI.result: The topological (anyon-like) features encoded in the coupling-dependent S-matrix phases play no role in the known entanglement measures computed at equilibrium in the ground state for an infinite system. The same conclusion holds for post-quench dynamics after a small quench of the topological parameter.
AI.conclusion: In the infinite-system regime, the anyon-like topological phases of the Federbush model do not manifest in the entanglement measures considered at equilibrium or in small quench dynamics of the topological parameter, suggesting these topological features are irrelevant to entanglement in this context.

title: A geometric origin for the radiative neutrino portal to secluded dark matter
comment: 57 pages and 7 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: We study a secluded dark-matter scenario in which the smallness of laboratory signals is linked to the origin of neutrino masses. In the four-dimensional theory, the dark sector contains a hidden scalar, a fermionic dark-matter particle, and heavy Majorana neutrinos. The same heavy-neutrino sector that generates light neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism also induces the Higgs-dark-scalar portal at one loop. This portal is tied to the small observed neutrino masses, naturally leading to very small Higgs-singlet mixing and suppressed signals in direct-detection and collider experiments. We then provide a geometric origin for the boundary condition of the tree level portal coupling being zero $κ(Λ_{\rm UV})=0$ via a five-dimensional sequestered setup. In this construction, the Standard Model fields and the hidden sector are localized on different branes, with sterile neutrinos propagating in the bulk. Five-dimensional locality forbids a fundamental local tree-level Higgs-dark-scalar contact interaction, while heavy-neutrino loops induce a small residual portal coupling. The main phenomenological parameter controlling the viability of the model is the heavy-neutrino mass scale: direct detection bounds it from above, while Big Bang nucleosynthesis bounds it from below through the requirement that the hidden scalar decays sufficiently early. Depending on the amount of five-dimensional sequestering, the viable region can span heavy-neutrino masses from the multi-TeV scale to the PeV scale, or even higher.

A five-dimensional sequestered setup provides a geometric origin for the zero tree-level portal coupling, with Standard Model fields and the hidden sector on separate branes and sterile neutrinos in the bulk. The viable parameter space is bounded by direct detection (above) and Big Bang nucleosynthesis (below) via the heavy-neutrino mass scale, spanning from multi-TeV to PeV scales or higher.

AI.conclusion: The model provides a geometrically motivated explanation for the suppressed dark-matter signals through their connection to neutrino mass generation, with the heavy-neutrino mass scale acting as the primary phenomenological control parameter determining the viable parameter space.

title: First Law of Proto-Area Entropy from Modular Spectral Geometry
comment: 10 pages, 3 figures; submitted to Eur. Phys. J. C
summary: We derive a first law of proto-area entropy in the CCKLP--Witten framework for approximate holographic entanglement wedge reconstruction. The central spectral function admits a modular Hamiltonian representation with kernel $L(x)=x\coth(x/2)$. For near-maximally-mixed bulk states, and within the unstructured Gaussian-unitary-ensemble (GUE) model of the encoding perturbation, the ensemble-averaged proto-area entropy varies linearly with bulk entropy to leading order, with a response coefficient containing a universal factor~$1/3$, traced to $L''(0)/2=1/6$ and independent of the bulk spectrum's detailed shape within this model. Imposing the gravitational-scaling condition required for nonzero backreaction, the first-law coefficient is $O(1)$, parametrically matching the semi-classical relation $δ({\rm Area}/4G_N)=δS_{\rm bulk}$.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a first law of proto-area entropy within the CCKLP–Witten framework for approximate holographic entanglement wedge reconstruction, showing that ensemble-averaged proto-area entropy varies linearly with bulk entropy with a universal 1/3 factor under the GUE model, and matches the semi-classical first law of entanglement when gravitational backreaction is included.
AI.motivation: To establish a thermodynamic/differential relation (a "first law") for the proto-area entropy in the approximate entanglement wedge reconstruction framework, connecting the spectral/modular structure of the encoding to bulk entropy and gravitational area.
AI.method: The derivation uses the CCKLP–Witten framework for approximate holographic entanglement wedge reconstruction. The central spectral function is expressed via a modular Hamiltonian with kernel L(x)=x·coth(x/2). The analysis focuses on near-maximally-mixed bulk states within an unstructured Gaussian-unitary-ensemble (GUE) model of the encoding perturbation. Ensemble averaging is performed, and a gravitational-scaling condition is imposed to ensure nonzero backreaction.

title: Quantum Tomography of Top Quarks as a Probe of Charge-Parity Violation

Using the first complete renormalized one-loop density matrix and the experimental covariance, we obtain complementary constraints comparable to those from direct tree-level $t\bar t H$ and $tH$ production.

title: BPS Invariants for Generalized Toric Calabi-Yau Threefolds

title: Molecular clouds constraints on sub-GeV DM and asteroid-mass PBHs
summary: We show that the ionization of molecular clouds provides a novel probe of dark matter scenarios producing low-energy $e^+e^-$ pairs through annihilation, decay, or Hawking evaporation of primordial black holes. By modeling the propagation of electrons and positrons inside molecular clouds, we show that uncertainties in charged-particle transport constitute the main limitation of this method. Nevertheless, for the most physically motivated propagation scenarios, the resulting constraints remain competitive with the strongest bounds currently available. We also identify the molecular-cloud properties that maximize the sensitivity to dark matter-induced ionization and discuss how larger samples of clouds, together with improved modeling of cosmic-ray ionization and cloud structure, could substantially enhance the reach of this technique. title: A Holographic Map from AdS$_3$ to CFT$_2$
summary: We propose a holographic map from the semiclassical Hilbert space of pure general relativity in $\text{AdS}_{3}$ to that of $\text{CFT}_{2}$. We define the bulk Hilbert space by semiclassically quantising the phase space in the basis of a fixed-area network on a Cauchy slice $Σ$. A fixed-area network is a maximal non-intersecting set of geodesics on $Σ$ whose lengths and angular momenta have been fixed. Our holographic map differentiates between `external' geodesics that are homotopic to a connected component of $\partial Σ$, and `internal' geodesics which are not. The lengths and angular momenta of external geodesics become conformal weights of primaries in the Hilbert space of the CFT living on the corresponding component of $\partial Σ$. The fixed-area network determines the wave function, which is given by a network of OPE coefficients of primaries whose weights are determined by the corresponding lengths. For sufficiently semiclassical states, there is an agreement between bulk and boundary inner products. We apply this proposal to various physics questions. The boundary dual of a bulk gauge turns out to be an emergent basis for sufficiently semiclassical states. We also define boundary operators that measure the lengths of geodesics behind the horizon, again in semiclassical states. Finally, we apply our map to closed universes and find a failure of semiclassicality in simple cases, which can be partially alleviated by the addition of a massive probe.

title: Dark Photon - ALP Freeze-in: 511 keV and H$α$ Constraints
summary: We investigate a freeze-in scenario of two component dark matter consisting of an axion-like particle (ALP) and a dark photon. The dark sector connects to the Standard Model through a dimension-five ALP-dark photon interaction, while a small kinetic mixing governs dark photon decays. Solving the coupled Boltzmann equations, we determine the parameter space consistent with the observed relic abundance. We find that, for a nearly degenerate dark sector, dark photon decay into an electron-positron pair through the kinetic mixing explains the Galactic 511 keV line while the dimension five operator can source the necessary production of dark photon and ALP particles to satisfy the relic density. We further confront the model with recent H$α$ observations of dwarf galaxies, together with constraints from the cosmic microwave background, diffuse gamma rays, direct detection and collider searches. We identify viable regions of parameter space yielding $Ω_{\rm DM}h^2\simeq0.12$, with an effective scale $Λ\sim10^{10}$-$10^{12}$ GeV, and dark photon lifetimes of order $10^{26}$-$10^{29}$ s, while remaining consistent with the observed 511 keV photon flux, $Hα$ constraints from Leo T and all other astrophysical constraints.

title: Tensionless limit of M5-brane and conformal symmetry of its bosonic body
summary: We obtain a tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane action and discuss its properties. The consistency of this limit requires that the field strength of the worldvolume 2-form gauge field on the M5 brane worldvolume is non-degenerate and never vanishes. Also the induced $6d$ worldvolume metric of this theory is non-degenerate in contrast to conventional tensionless (null) $p$-branes. We find that the tensionless M5-brane action is invariant under a super-Weyl symmetry acting on the bulk supergeometry, while in the purely bosonic case the action is invariant under an 11D target-space conformal symmetry, a property which is characteristic for the tensionless bosonic branes. Upon imposing a static gauge, which fixes worldvolume diffeomorphisms, this 11D conformal symmetry becomes a deformed 6d worldovolume conformal symmetry whose action on the worldvolume coordinates involves field dependent terms. When the transversal fluctuations of the 5-brane in the bulk are zero, the model reduces to the conformal non-linear chiral 2-form electrodynamics considered earlier by Gibbons and West, and by Townsend.

title: Dark Photon Dark Matter from Quantum Fluctuations during Starobinsky Inflation
summary: We present a detailed investigation of scenarios in which dark-photon dark matter is produced from quantum fluctuations during inflation. In particular, we focus on inflationary models that necessarily involve a Weyl transformation, dependent on the inflaton amplitude, in order to move to the Einstein frame. In such models, the kinetic function of the longitudinal mode of the dark photon varies throughout, and even after, the inflationary period. We show that this variation of the kinetic function has a substantial impact on the resulting relic abundance of dark photons. As a representative and phenomenologically important example, we analyze the Starobinsky inflation model, for which we perform an accurate computation of the relic dark-photon abundance. By imposing the relevant observational constraints, we find that, in order to reproduce the observed dark-matter density in the present Universe, the dark-photon mass must lie in the range $5.6 < m < 7.4\,μ\mathrm{eV}$ within the framework considered in this work.

title: Holographic timelike complexity for de Sitter

summary: We investigate the recent proposal of holographic volume complexity for timelike subregions \cite{Alishahiha:2025xml} in the framework of static patch holography for de Sitter spacetime. Using the stretched-horizon prescription, we compute the timelike subregion complexity as a function of the subregion duration for pure de Sitter and Schwarzschild de Sitter geometries. In pure de Sitter spacetime, the timelike subregion complexity displays exponential growth for short durations, and hyperfast growth near a maximal duration, paralleling the features of spacelike volume complexity \cite{Jorstad:2022mls}. For Schwarzschild de Sitter, when the stretched horizon is near the cosmological horizon, the behavior broadly remains similar to pure de Sitter. However, when the stretched horizon is near the black hole horizon, the hyperfast growth for long durations is replaced by nonlinear growth regime. Along the way, we also compute the corresponding timelike holographic entanglement entropy for de Sitter and Schwarzschild de Sitter.

title: Pentaquark Bound States and Regge Trajectories in QCD via Bethe Salpeter Formalism
summary: We present a comprehensive calculation of pentaquark masses and Regge trajectories within the framework of the Godfrey-Isgur relativized quark model. The pentaquark is treated as a meson-baryon molecular system, and the bound state is solved using the Bethe-Salpeter equation with the effective meson-baryon interaction motivated by GI, including smearing, running coupling, and spin-spin interactions. Using the latest PDG data for the known Pc and Pcs states, we compute the ground state and first two radial excitations for four pentaquark candidates: Pc(4440), Pc(4457), Pcs(4338), and Pcs(4459). The calculated masses are in excellent agreement with experiment. We also construct radial Regge trajectories in the (n, M^2) plane. Within the three calculated radial levels, the trajectories are approximately linear, with slopes comparable to those reported for ordinary hadrons. These results are consistent with a common confinement-driven pattern, but do not establish its universality.

title: A-type Sigma Models from Differential Poisson Geometry
summary: We study the differential Poisson sigma model (DPSM) in the symplectic case and show that its classical reduction defines a distinguished class of A-type models on symplectic targets, not necessarily Kähler. The DPSM is a covariant first-order sigma model whose graded target is the parity-shifted tangent bundle $T[1]M$ of a Poisson manifold $M$. Its graded Poisson tensor encodes a differential Poisson bracket on $C(T[1]M)\congΩ^\bullet(M)$, written covariantly in terms of a connection $Γ$ and its transpose $\widetildeΓ$. In the nondegenerate case, the Jacobi identities force $Γ$ to be flat, while the quartic coupling of the reduced action is given by the curvature of $\widetildeΓ$, induced by the torsion of $Γ$. Thus, the DPSM selects a symplectic class in which the A-model curvature coupling acquires a first-order Poisson origin. We describe this class through examples and obstructions; $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and K3 surfaces are excluded, while affine symplectic targets, symplectic tori, and the Kodaira--Thurston manifold furnish explicit examples. The graded parent geometry on $T[1]M$ equips $Ω^\bullet(M)$ with a differential Poisson bracket and $Ω^\bullet(M)[1]$ with a strict $L_\infty$-algebra structure, equipping the observable complex with a natural chain-level differential Poisson structure that is not manifest in the usual Kähler formulation of the A-model.

title: Rare processes in ultrahigh-energy tau-lepton transport
summary: In cosmic neutrino observatories, charged-lepton transport is a key input for interpreting observables and reconstructing neutrino events. Charged leptons propagating through matter undergo several energy loss processes, such as electron pair production and photonuclear interaction. In this work, we investigate several rare processes in tau-lepton transport, focusing primarily on muon pair production, $τN \to τμ^+μ^- N$, and Primakoff neutral-pion production, $τN \to τπ^0 N$. At EeV energies, we find that the energy loss contributions from muon pair and Primakoff pion production are only $0.6\%$ and $0.2\%$, respectively, of that from electron pair production. Nevertheless, dimuon production may be relevant to tau neutrino searches in underwater and under-ice Cherenkov telescopes. The interaction length for dimuon emission by an EeV tau is only $6~{\rm km}$ in standard rock. Such events may be identified through the lateral separation of dimuon tracks or through a kebab topology if tau decays in the detector.

title: Weak Bose-Einstein condensation in a rigidly rotating magnetized charged Bose gas
summary: We investigate the weak Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) scenario of a noninteracting charged Bose gas simultaneously subjected to a strong magnetic field and rigid rotation. Using standard methods of finite-temperature quantum field theory and the generalized Fock-Schwinger formalism, we derive the corresponding thermodynamic potential in the nonrelativistic and lowest Landau level approximations. An appropriate modification of the effective chemical potential yields a consistent thermodynamic description and naturally introduces a magnetorotational fugacity. Within the high-temperature approximation, rigid rotation enters the thermodynamics solely through the Tolman-Ehrenfest local temperature. We demonstrate that rigid rotation does not qualitatively modify the weak BEC scenario induced by Landau quantization. The magnetorotational fugacity remains below unity throughout the phenomenologically relevant temperature range, while the continuous evolution of the ground state population and the absence of a singularity in the specific heat provide complementary signatures of the persistence of weak BEC. We further study the thermodynamic properties of the system under conditions relevant to quark-gluon plasma and neutron-star matter. We show that rotational effects are much more pronounced in the former. Our analysis reveals a new magnetic response to rigid rotation: while magnetic fields enhance diamagnetism, rotation drives it toward paramagnetism. This behavior reflects a competition between magnetic quantization and rotational orbital motion, emphasizing the role of rotation in shaping the magnetic response of bosonic matter.

title: Classification of minimal models producing b, c and tau masses at one-loop level
summary: The Standard Model neither provides a dynamical explanation for the quark and lepton mass hierarchies, nor a rationale for why all of these masses save that of the top quark are suppressed compared to the electroweak scale. Motivated by this, we explore the alternative radiative mass generation hypothesis, specialising to the generation of the bottom, charm, and tau masses at one-loop level. A classification of all minimal models that use exotic scalars and exotic fermions only is presented, resulting in 25 possibilities featuring four exotic multiplets. As a bonus, some of the models produce a one-loop neutrino Dirac mass if a right-handed neutrino field is included, and some feature WIMP-like dark matter candidates. By way of example, we analyse the phenomenology of a benchmark model chosen from the set of 25 candidates and find that it is capable of exactly replicating the predicted Standard Model Yukawa couplings within the permitted parameter space.

title: The price for monopole dark matter
summary: We construct an explicit model where dark matter consists of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles. The dark sector is in thermal contact with the Standard Model, and dark monopoles are created by a thermal phase transition in the early Universe. Generically, the abundance of monopoles is negligible with respect to that of stable dark elementary particles. We show how to avoid this by taking the lightest stable particle, a dark fermion, sufficiently light for its abundance to be suppressed, yet heavy enough to satisfy constraints on dark radiation. In this specific window of parameters, dark matter is composed of monopoles with a mass of about $10^8$ GeV or larger, depending on the nature of the phase transition. This candidate lies beyond the reach of present, conventional dark-matter detection experiments. However, the model necessarily predicts dark radiation, with $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ close to present-day bounds. In addition, if the dark phase transition is strongly first order, we find that the corresponding gravitational wave spectrum lies close to the region probed by future interferometers.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs an explicit model where dark matter consists of 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles produced by a thermal phase transition in a dark sector in thermal contact with the Standard Model. The monopole abundance can dominate if a stable dark fermion is made sufficiently light (to suppress its abundance) yet heavy enough to avoid dark radiation constraints. This yields monopole dark matter with mass ≳10^8 GeV, which is beyond conventional detection, but the model necessarily predicts dark radiation (ΔN_eff near current bounds) and, if the transition is strongly first order, gravitational waves detectable by future interferometers.
AI.motivation: To provide a viable, explicit particle-physics model of dark matter as topological monopoles, overcoming the generic problem that monopole abundance is negligible compared to stable dark elementary particles, while making the scenario testable through dark radiation and gravitational wave signatures.
AI.method: Construct a dark sector in thermal contact with the Standard Model where 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles are produced via a thermal phase transition. The abundance of the lightest stable particle (a dark fermion) is suppressed by tuning its mass low enough, while keeping it heavy enough to satisfy dark radiation constraints, thereby allowing monopoles to dominate dark matter.
AI.result: In the viable parameter window, dark matter is composed of monopoles with mass about 10^8 GeV or larger, depending on the nature of the phase transition. The model predicts dark radiation with ΔN_eff close to present bounds, and if the dark phase transition is strongly first order, the gravitational wave spectrum is near the sensitivity of future interferometers.
AI.conclusion: Monopole dark matter is a plausible and explicit construction, but it lies beyond current detection experiments. It is indirectly testable via dark radiation measurements and future gravitational wave observatories.

title: pylhe: A Lightweight Python interface to Les Houches Event files
comment: 4 pages, submitted to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS)
summary: Les Houches Event files are a standard format for Monte Carlo event generators in high-energy physics. pylhe is a lightweight pure-Python library for reading and writing LHE event data. It supports .lhe and compressed .lhe.gz files, implements the widely used LHE 3.0 features including multiple event weights and generator metadata, and also supports the recent HDF5-based LHEH5 format. By exposing events through a pythonic iterator and shared data structures, pylhe enables memory-efficient processing of large event samples without loading entire files into memory. The library also supports format conversion and integration with modern analysis workflows, including columnar analysis with Awkward Array and downstream machine-learning applications.

AI.tldr: pylhe is a lightweight pure-Python library for reading and writing Les Houches Event (LHE) files, supporting LHE 3.0 features, compressed .lhe.gz files, and the HDF5-based LHEH5 format, with memory-efficient streaming and integration with Awkward Array and machine-learning workflows.
AI.motivation: Monte Carlo event generators in high-energy physics produce LHE files as a standard format, but there is a need for a lightweight, memory-efficient Python tool to read, write, and convert these files that integrates with modern analysis workflows.
AI.method: pylhe implements a pythonic iterator interface over shared data structures for streaming event data, supports LHE 3.0 features (multiple event weights, generator metadata), handles .lhe and .lhe.gz files, supports the LHEH5 HDF5 format, and provides format conversion capabilities with integration into Awkward Array and downstream ML applications.

title: Halbach Magnetic Weber Bars
summary: Magnetic Weber Bars have been proposed to search for gravitational waves in the kHz to GHz regime by exploiting the mechanical deformation of a large magnet induced by a gravitational wave. Here we propose to increase the effectiveness of such devices by considering magnetic field configurations with strong gradients, albeit lower field strengths, such as Halbach arrays. We focus on one of the most challenging but most realistic signals, with short duration and low coherence, exploiting the ring-down period of the mechanical resonator. We show that with demonstrated technology this setup can reach sensitivities of $S_h^{1/2} \simeq 10^{-21}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ at a broad set of frequencies around several resonance peaks at $\sim 10$ kHz, and $S_h^{1/2} \simeq 5 \cdot 10^{-20}/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ in a broadband search at higher frequencies. We discuss plausible upgrades to reach $S_h^{1/2} \simeq (10^{-23} - 10^{-21})/\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ in a broadband search covering 10 kHz - MHz.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using Halbach arrays (magnetic field configurations with strong gradients but lower field strengths) to improve Magnetic Weber Bar gravitational wave detectors targeting the kHz to GHz regime, achieving sensitivities around 10^-21/√Hz near several resonance peaks at ~10 kHz with demonstrated technology, and discussing upgrades to reach 10^-23 to 10^-21/√Hz across 10 kHz - MHz.
AI.motivation: Magnetic Weber Bars have been proposed for gravitational wave detection in the kHz to GHz regime using mechanical deformation of large magnets. The authors aim to increase the effectiveness of such devices by exploring alternative magnetic field configurations, particularly focusing on realistic short-duration, low-coherence signals.
AI.method: The authors propose replacing traditional magnetic field configurations with Halbach arrays, which provide strong field gradients at lower field strengths. They exploit the ring-down period of the mechanical resonator to detect short-duration, low-coherence signals. Sensitivity calculations are performed for realistic signal scenarios.
AI.result: With demonstrated technology, the setup can reach sensitivities of S_h^{1/2} ≈ 10^-21/√Hz at a broad set of frequencies around several resonance peaks at ~10 kHz, and S_h^{1/2} ≈ 5·10^-20/√Hz in a broadband search at higher frequencies. Plausible upgrades could reach S_h^{1/2} ≈ (10^-23 - 10^-21)/√Hz across 10 kHz - MHz.
AI.conclusion: Halbach array configurations can significantly enhance the sensitivity of Magnetic Weber Bar gravitational wave detectors, particularly for realistic short-duration, low-coherence signals, with demonstrated technology already achieving competitive sensitivities and promising upgrade paths offering further improvements across a broad frequency range.

title: The fundamental limit of jet tagging: Beyond top jets
summary: Jet tagging, i.e. determining the origin of high-energy hadronic jets, is a key challenge in particle physics. Machine-learning-based taggers have achieved remarkable progress, raising the question of how close current methods are to the theoretical limit of performance. Previous work addressed this question for boosted top-quark jets using transformer-based generative models that provide realistic synthetic jet data with known probability density functions. This enables a direct comparison between modern taggers and the optimal likelihood-ratio classifier. In this note, we summarize the approach and extend the study to boosted W, Z, and H$\rightarrow gg$ jets. We find that the gap to the estimated optimal limit is strongly jet dependent and is substantially reduced for these seemingly more challenging tagging tasks. Ongoing work aimed at understanding the interpretation, robustness, and scaling of these limits is also briefly discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates how close modern machine-learning jet taggers are to the theoretical optimal performance limit by using transformer-based generative models to produce realistic synthetic jets with known probability densities. The study extends earlier top-quark jet analysis to W, Z, and H→gg jets, finding that the gap to the optimal limit is strongly jet-dependent and much smaller for these more challenging tagging tasks.
AI.motivation: To quantify the gap between current machine-learning jet taggers and the theoretical optimal performance limit, thereby assessing how much room for improvement remains in jet tagging algorithms.
AI.method: Uses transformer-based generative models to generate realistic synthetic jet data with known probability density functions, enabling direct comparison between modern taggers and the optimal likelihood-ratio classifier. The approach is extended from top-quark jets to boosted W, Z, and H→gg jets.
AI.result: The gap between modern taggers and the estimated optimal limit is strongly jet-dependent and substantially reduced for W, Z, and H→gg jets compared to top-quark jets, despite these being seemingly more challenging tagging tasks.
AI.conclusion: Current jet taggers perform closer to the theoretical limit for W/Z/H→gg tagging than for top-quark tagging; ongoing work aims to understand the interpretation, robustness, and scaling of these limits.

title: Penumbral Inflation from Calabi-Yau Boundaries

summary: Mapping Calabi-Yau geometry to early Universe cosmology remains a primary goal in string phenomenology. We present an inflationary mechanism where flux stationarity shifts the field dynamics, driving inflation along the volume-controlling saxion direction near a Hodge boundary. In this region, the internal geometry strictly dictates the scalar potential. This setup stabilizes the field against heavy moduli corrections without consuming extra flux tadpoles. As a result, the properties of the geometric boundary translate directly into primordial tensor perturbations, creating a clear physical link from string compactifications to measurable data. The resulting geometric predictions match current cosmic microwave background limits and provide specific, testable targets for upcoming LiteBIRD and CMB-S4 observations.

The internal geometry strictly dictates the scalar potential in this region, stabilizing the field without extra flux tadpoles. The geometric boundary properties translate directly into primordial tensor perturbations, creating a link from string compactifications to observable cosmology, with predictions matching current CMB limits and offering testable targets for LiteBIRD and CMB-S4.

title: New $CP$ sum rules from exact $U$-spin degeneracy
summary: We propose a new class of $CP$ sum rules in the $U$-spin limit, based on the observation that the weak phase in the Standard Model can be removed in the degenerate limit $m_d=m_s$. Unlike previous $U$-spin analyses formulated at the amplitude level, our sum rules are expressed directly in terms of decay widths. They apply to matched partial waves, spin observables, and angular moments and include nonpairwise cases beyond the usual single-insertion $d\leftrightarrow s$ relation.

AI.motivation: Previous U-spin analyses were formulated at the amplitude level and limited to pairwise d↔s relations. This work seeks a more general framework that works directly with measurable decay widths and extends beyond pairwise cases to broader observables.
AI.method: The method exploits the fact that in the U-spin limit (degenerate md=ms), the Standard Model weak phase can be removed, leading to new CP sum rules expressed directly in terms of decay widths rather than amplitudes. The sum rules are derived to apply to matched partial waves, spin observables, and angular moments, and include non-pairwise cases beyond the usual single-insertion d↔s relation.

AI.conclusion: The proposed CP sum rules offer a more general and directly measurable framework for testing CP violation in the U-spin limit, extending beyond amplitude-level pairwise relations to width-level constraints covering a richer set of observables.

title: Inflation and Reheating by Dynamical Torsion
summary: In gravity theories with torsion, inflation can be driven by the dynamical torsion. Since it naturally has a derivative coupling to the axial current consisting of Standard Model particles, the reheating dynamics should be much different from conventional inflation models like Starobinsky inflation. We calculate the inflaton decay rate in detail and find that, although the 2 body decay into the fermion pair is vanishing in the massless fermion limit, the anomaly-induced 2 body decay into the gauge bosons and 3 body decay involving the Higgs boson are non-vanishing and they give sizable contributions to the total decay width of the inflaton. This gives a natural lower bound on the reheating temperature in the inflation model with dynamical torsion.

AI.tldr: In gravity theories with torsion, inflation is driven by dynamical torsion, which couples derivatively to the axial current of Standard Model particles. This paper calculates the inflaton decay rate in detail, finding that while 2-body decay into fermion pairs vanishes in the massless limit, anomaly-induced 2-body decay into gauge bosons and 3-body decay involving the Higgs boson are non-vanishing and contribute significantly to the total decay width, thereby providing a natural lower bound on the reheating temperature.
AI.motivation: The reheating dynamics in gravity theories with dynamical torsion are expected to differ significantly from conventional inflation models like Starobinsky inflation, due to the intrinsic derivative coupling between torsion and the axial current of Standard Model particles. A detailed understanding of the inflaton decay rate is needed to determine the reheating temperature and constrain the model.
AI.method: The authors calculate the inflaton decay rate in detail, considering both 2-body decays (into fermion pairs and into gauge bosons via anomaly) and 3-body decays involving the Higgs boson, evaluating their contributions to the total decay width.
AI.result: The 2-body decay into a fermion pair vanishes in the massless fermion limit, but anomaly-induced 2-body decay into gauge bosons and 3-body decay involving the Higgs boson are non-vanishing and give sizable contributions to the total inflaton decay width.
AI.conclusion: The non-vanishing decay channels provide a natural lower bound on the reheating temperature in the inflation model with dynamical torsion, distinguishing it from conventional inflation scenarios.

title: Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC
summary: We study the phenomenology of light scalar sgoldstinos, with masses from the dimuon threshold up to a few GeV, focusing on their production and detection prospects at the SND@HL-LHC experiment. We review the effective sgoldstino interactions with Standard Model particles, the dominant meson-decay production channels, and the relevant experimental constraints on the model parameter space. We also outline the recently proposed SND@HL-LHC detector configuration and discuss the kinematics and track separation of the muon pair produced in sgoldstino decays inside the detector volume. For two representative sets of supersymmetry-breaking parameters, we present sensitivity estimates and show that the muon-antimuon separation efficiency should be taken into account in searches for the dimuon signal.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the phenomenology of light scalar sgoldstinos (masses from dimuon threshold to a few GeV) at the SND@HL-LHC experiment, reviewing their effective interactions, meson-decay production channels, experimental constraints, and presenting sensitivity estimates for two representative supersymmetry-breaking scenarios. It highlights that muon-antimuon separation efficiency must be accounted for in dimuon searches.
AI.motivation: To investigate the discovery potential of the proposed SND@HL-LHC detector for light scalar sgoldstinos produced via meson decays, and to assess how the kinematics and track separation of the resulting muon pairs affect experimental sensitivity.
AI.method: The authors review the effective sgoldstino interactions with Standard Model particles and dominant meson-decay production channels. They outline the SND@HL-LHC detector configuration and analyze the kinematics and track separation of muon pairs from sgoldstino decays inside the detector volume. Sensitivity estimates are computed for two representative sets of supersymmetry-breaking parameters.
AI.result: For two representative supersymmetry-breaking scenarios, sensitivity estimates are presented, demonstrating that the muon-antimuon separation efficiency significantly affects the searches for the dimuon signal and must be incorporated into the analysis.
AI.conclusion: The SND@HL-LHC offers promising prospects for detecting light scalar sgoldstinos, but the muon-pair track-separation efficiency is a crucial experimental factor that must be properly modeled when searching for the dimuon signature.

title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
summary: We reconsider the production of dark photons $A'$ as dark matter, from the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field $h$, that is stochastically misaligned from the minimum of its potential during inflation. This is a simple and predictive framework for generating the $A'$ relic abundance. It is constrained by structure formation, since the $A'$ are initially boosted, and inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which require small quartic couplings $λh^4$. We identify $A'$ masses between 100 eV and 1 GeV and gauge couplings $g\sim 10^{-15}-10^{-10}$ that are consistent in this scenario, and which become more tightly constrained if a generic level of kinetic mixing is present. The favored parameter region could be tested through future CMB or Lyman-$α$ observations, and, in the presence of kinetic mixing, by direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches.

AI.tldr: This paper reconsiders dark photon dark matter production via perturbative decay of a stochastically misaligned dark Higgs field during inflation, identifying a viable parameter space of A' masses (100 eV to 1 GeV) and gauge couplings (g ~ 10^-15 to 10^-10) consistent with structure formation and isocurvature constraints, testable by future CMB, Lyman-α, direct detection, and gamma-ray observations.
AI.motivation: To provide a simple and predictive framework for generating the dark photon relic abundance as dark matter, while identifying the parameter space consistent with cosmological constraints such as structure formation and inflationary isocurvature fluctuations.
AI.method: The framework posits a dark Higgs field stochastically misaligned from its potential minimum during inflation, which perturbatively decays into dark photons A'. Constraints from structure formation (since A' are initially boosted) and inflationary isocurvature fluctuations (requiring small quartic couplings λh^4) are applied to identify the allowed parameter space, including the effect of generic kinetic mixing.
AI.result: The scenario is consistent for A' masses between 100 eV and 1 GeV with gauge couplings g ~ 10^-15 to 10^-10. The allowed region becomes more tightly constrained if generic kinetic mixing is present. The favored parameter region is testable through future CMB or Lyman-α observations, and via direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches if kinetic mixing exists.
AI.conclusion: A stochastic misalignment production mechanism for dark photons from dark Higgs decay provides a viable and predictive dark matter framework, with a constrained but testable parameter space that can be probed by upcoming cosmological and particle physics experiments.
